title: kg/1-health — a health record in kg/1
description: The machine-readable form of docs/DATA-CONTRACT.md. A document whose meta.app is health-viewer must match this schema; the base kg/1 format is thin on purpose (any kind, any key) and this file is the health profile that makes it strict. What JSON Schema cannot state — that a node's `source` names a document in the same document, that an edge's ends carry the kinds its relation allows, that a prediction is about a condition or an observation in this document and never about a date before its own, that only a node that can be in force may carry a validity window — is in scripts/lib/kg-contract.ts, which is the validator that reads this file.
x-contract-source: docs/DATA-CONTRACT.md (rev 5, T06 event model, T18 predictions)
x-contract-change: 2.1.0 — T18: a `prediction` is a simulation with a shape — `target` (what it is about), `horizon` (the date it is about), `condition` (the predicate it waits on), `delta_median` (the change it would make), `source` and `confidence` — and no `when`, because its date is the horizon. 2.0.0 — T06: `source` is renamed to `document` (the document is the provenance and has the date printed on it), `procedure` becomes its own event kind, and the six event kinds are the spine of the model: condition, observation, encounter, medication, procedure, document. A summary and a prediction stay non-events (a marker and a simulation).
x-contract-snapshot: There is no stored snapshot shape. A snapshot is derived, not recorded: the state at date D is every node whose `when` is on or before D plus every edge whose validity window holds at D (DATA-CONTRACT §Temporal rule). The immutable snapshot store is proposal T08, explicitly not approved (PLAN §B2), so this contract covers the snapshot by making that derivation well-defined — an event always has a date, and a temporary relation is closed with valid_from/valid_to instead of deleted.

when.description: the date a thing happened — a point, or an interval {from, to} for something that lasts

nonEmptyText.description: a string with something in it. Both readers of this contract trim before they answer — `isNonEmptyString` in scripts/lib/kg-contract.ts, `conditionProblems` in src/rules.ts, `loadPredictions` in src/prediction.ts — so a string of spaces is empty to them, while a bare `minLength: 1` counts it as content. A document this file accepted would then be thrown out by the loader, which is the disagreement this gate exists to prevent, so the rule is spelled once here and referred to by the fields that are read that way: a node id, a fact name, a forecast's target and source, and the two ends of an edge.

not.description: must not be blank — an empty or whitespace-only string names nothing

factValue.description: one value a fact may hold, and so one value a comparison may compare it with

predicate.description: a condition over the facts of a record — one comparison, or a group of them joined by all / any / not. Deliberately the same vocabulary a rule uses (src/rules.ts): a rule's `when` and a prediction's `condition` are one language, so the engine that decides whether a rule fires decides whether a forecast is live. A condition is about facts — `age`, `current_smoker`, `ldl_cholesterol` — and never about time; dates live on nodes. What a comparison's `value` may be is decided operator by operator, because the engine (`conditionProblems`) refuses an `exists` that carries a value and a list where one value belongs: a condition this file accepts is a condition the engine reads, and one it refuses is refused here first.

oneOf.description: one comparison: a fact, an operator, and the value it is compared with

op.description: eq, ne, lt, le, gt, ge compare one value; `in` takes a non-empty list; `exists` asks only whether the fact is known

oneOf.description: eq: the fact equals one value
ne: the fact is not one value
lt: the fact is below one value
le: the fact is at or below one value
gt: the fact is above one value
ge: the fact is at or above one value
in: the fact is one of a non-empty list of values
exists: the fact is known — the operator asks whether it is there, so it takes no value

not.description: exists takes no value — it asks only whether the fact is there

oneOf.description: all of these comparisons hold
at least one of these comparisons holds
this comparison does not hold

colors.description: kind → hex; health kinds ship defaults, a document may override them

meta.description: the envelope; identity lives in meta.profile and nowhere else

profile.description: sex and year of birth are data, never a constant in the template; a full date and a name are optional

node.description: eight kinds, six of them events. An event is a fact in the record with a date in `when` and, unless it is the document itself, a `source` naming the document it came from. A summary is a virtual marker and a prediction is a simulation: both are visible, neither is an event. Fields outside this list are carried through untouched, which is how the viewer gains a key without the contract changing — and a field the contract puts on one kind (an observation's value, a condition's status) is typed only where the contract puts it.

id.description: unique and stable; never reused for different content

kind.description: eight kinds, no free-form ones: the template has a layout for each and nothing for the rest. Six of them are events: condition, observation, encounter, medication, procedure, document

confirmed.description: true when a human confirmed it; otherwise false and the UI says "not confirmed"

source.description: id of the document node this fact came from; a document node carries none, because it is the provenance

oneOf.description: a condition needs the date it started, its status and the document it came from
an observation needs its date, its value, its unit and the document it came from

value.description: a number, not a string: "4.9 mmol/L" cannot be plotted, sorted or compared

unit.description: UCUM code where one exists (mmol/L, mm[Hg])

flag.description: as the lab printed it, never derived

oneOf.description: an encounter needs its date and the document it came from
a medication needs the date it started, its status and the document it came from
a procedure needs the date it was performed and the document it came from

code.description: SNOMED CT, ICD-10-PCS or OPCS-4 — as the document printed it

oneOf.description: a document needs the date printed on it: it is the provenance every other fact points at, so it has none of its own

link.description: where the file lives, relative to the document (sources/discharge-2021-05-14.pdf)

not.description: a document node is the provenance, it does not point at one

oneOf.description: a summary needs the end of the period it rolls up and the document it came from

origin.description: a generated summary never looks like a doctor's

oneOf.description: a prediction is a simulation, not a fact: it needs what it is about, the date it is about, the condition it waits on and the median change it would make

target.description: id of the condition or observation this forecast is about

horizon.description: the date the forecast is about — not the day it was made, which is the date printed on its source document

condition.description: the condition that has to be met before this forecast may move an estimate

delta_median.description: the median change the forecast would make to the estimate of its scale, in that scale's unit, once its condition is met

not.description: a prediction is not an event: its date is the horizon, and a second date in `when` would be the second kind of time this contract exists to prevent

oneOf.description: an immunization is a dose given on a day, with the document that recorded it; it is not a procedure — the two are kept apart because a card lists them apart
a device is in or on the person from a date; it carries the datasheet it was fitted from, and the limits it imposes

link.description: the datasheet — the manufacturer's page or PDF describing what this thing is and what it forbids

oneOf.description: an allergy or an intolerance: a reaction, when it was first recorded, and whether it still stands

edge.description: a relation. `source` and `confidence` are carried when they are known; `valid_from`/`valid_to` when the relation itself is temporary — a relation that was true between two dates and is not true now is still a fact about the past, so it is closed, not deleted.

label.description: the relation; the list is closed, and a new relation needs an entry in docs/DATA-CONTRACT.md first

source.description: id of the document node this relation came from
